note: Ahmad 1965 redescribes the alate and the soldier from Thai specimens and gives measurements; the original description is that of Haviland 1898 (not obtained), so this entry follows the redescription.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown; reddish brown around the antennal sockets and on both sides of the postclypeus; anteclypeus tinged yellowish brown; labrum pale brown; mandibles reddish brown with the teeth darker; antennae pale brown, the tip of each segment whitish; pronotum reddish brown; tibiae and tarsi yellowish brown; wing membrane pale smoky brown. Hairs on the head sparse; a few short hairs at the tip of the labrum; a row of short hairs on the anterior margin of the pronotum, long setae and short hairs on the lateral margins, and a few scattered setae on the disc. The head is nearly circular, the Y-shaped suture indistinct. The compound eyes are moderately projecting and not circular; the eye suture is distinct. The ocelli are small, broadly oval to nearly circular, and touch the compound eye. The labrum is broad and dome-shaped, its sides converging posteriorly. The antennae have 11 segments, segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3 and as long as segment 4. The pronotum is narrower than the head, its anterior margin indistinctly concave, the lateral margins weakly convex, the anterolateral corners narrowly rounded.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head reddish brown, the frons dark brown; mandibles dark reddish brown; labrum and antennae pale brown; pronotum slightly paler than the head. Hairs on the head sparse; long and short setae on the lateral margins and disc of the pronotum. The head is short, the frons weakly projecting forwards; the frontal projections are distinct, high and broadly rounded; in profile the upper half of the frons is nearly vertical and the lower half slopes gradually. The compound eyes are small and oval, 0.11—0.13 mm from the antennal sockets. The labrum is ligulate and reaches three quarters of the mandibles. The mandibles are short with a basal swelling; the left mandible has 3 marginal teeth; the right mandible has 2 marginal teeth. The postmentum is twice as long as its maximum width, narrowest at the posterior end. The antennae are short, with 10 segments, segment 3 the shortest. The pronotum is as wide as the head and nearly rectangular; its anterior margin very shallowly concave, its posterior margin straight, its sides parallel and its anterolateral corners broadly rounded.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements (mm, range, mean in parentheses). Alates, 5 individuals: head length to the tip of the labrum 0.90—1.00 (0.96); head length to the base of the mandibles 0.68—0.75 (0.73); head width 0.79—0.82 (0.79); long diameter of the compound eye 0.21—0.23 (0.22); short diameter of the compound eye 0.18—0.19 (0.18); from the lower margin of the compound eye to the lower margin of the head 0.11—0.16 (0.13); ocellus length 0.06—0.07 (0.06); ocellus width 0.05 (mean); pronotum length 0.39—0.43 (0.42); pronotum width 0.64—0.72 (0.67). Soldiers, 10 individuals: head length to the base of the mandibles 1.06—1.11 (1.08); head width 0.86—0.90 (0.88); head height 0.54—0.57 (0.56); compound eye length 0.09—0.10 (0.09); compound eye width 0.05—0.07 (0.06); length of the left mandible 0.54—0.57 (0.56); distance from the first marginal tooth of the left mandible to the apical tooth 0.11—0.12 (0.11); postmentum length 0.64—0.68 (0.66); maximum width of the postmentum 0.32—0.34 (0.32); minimum width of the postmentum 0.23—0.25 (0.24); pronotum length 0.43—0.46 (0.44); pronotum width 0.82—0.90 (0.87). Specimens examined were collected in Thailand at Prew (1962-03-30, in a log) and at Tung Sa-Lang Luang (1962-04-10, in an intact part of a log, with queen, alates, soldiers and nymphs).
